newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB-Russian sugar beet plantings to edge up.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Russian sugar beet plantings to edge up.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.

MOSCOW, March 20 - SovEcon anticipates that the downward trend in Russian sugarbeet plantings will level off and that the sugarbeet area in 1997 may increase to 1.1-1.15 million hectares, mainly in the major producing areas like Central Chernozem (Black Earth) and the Northern Caucasus.
The government's program for sugar production development stipulates an increase in the use of mineral fertilizers and pesticides this year.
But the costs of sugarbeet production in Russia remain abnormally high, while productivity continues to decline.
Refined sugar produced domestically is less competitive against imported sugar, particularly from Ukraine.
An excess of sugar supplies on the domestic market, caused by increased imports, affected both sugar refineries and sugarbeet producers last year.
Local sugarbeet producers can only partly meet the demand of domestic refineries, while 50 to 60 percent of domestic demand is covered by imports of raw sugar.
